sections.heading: Repair or Replace an East Orange Roof? The 25% Rule and 20-Year-Old Asphalt Shingle Roofs

c.v: Should a 20-year-old roof be replaced? Not on age alone.

runs.v: Many asphalt shingle roofs are designed for roughly 20 to 30 years, so the inspection's focus is condition: curling, granule loss, and cracked shingles across the roof point to replacement, while isolated damage points to repair. A new installation with GAF or Owens Corning shingles, which offer 50-year manufacturer warranty options, resets the clock.

c.v: What is the 25% rule for roofing?

runs.v: Once damage covers more than about 25% of the roof, replacement usually makes more sense than another repair. In New Jersey, repairing more than 25% of the roof area in 12 months also needs a permit under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7 on any building but a detached one- or two-family home.

faqs.q: How often should you inspect a roof in East Orange or Essex County?

runs.v: The NRCA recommends a roof inspection at least twice per year, spring and fall, the ideal seasons in New Jersey, plus an additional inspection after any major weather event. At a minimum, homeowners should inspect roofs at least once a year and get a professional inspection at least once every two years; annual inspections are advised for roofs nearing the end of their lifespan, and roofs older than 15 years should be inspected more often than once a year. Proper maintenance on that cadence extends asphalt-shingle service life by roughly 25–30%, per ARMA.

faqs.q: Do you coordinate tenant access for inspections on East Orange rental properties?

runs.v: Yes. Newark Quality Roofing schedules top-floor interior checks on an East Orange property through the owner or property manager, with the advance notice New Jersey landlord-tenant law requires.

faqs.q: Does a roof inspection in East Orange trigger a permit?

runs.v: No, an inspection triggers no permit on its own. If it leads to work, re-roofing a detached one- or two-family house is ordinary maintenance under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7, so that standard residential reroofing needs no permit, while larger residential and commercial roofs follow the permit rules.

faqs.q: What does infrared scanning detect on an East Orange flat roof that a visual inspection misses?

runs.v: Infrared thermal imaging detects moisture trapped in the insulation beneath the membrane, moisture invisible during a visual surface inspection. EPDM and TPO are common materials for flat roofing systems, along with modified bitumen, and a scan can flag wet insulation under any of them.

faqs.q: Does a roof inspection on an East Orange Register-listed building need historic approval?

runs.v: No. An inspection only looks at and documents the roof; if the report leads to repair or replacement on a Register-listed building, confirm any review requirements with the City of East Orange before work begins.
